candidates.change_summary: Replace the returned bytes4 selector with a different valid bytes4 constant that still passes ERC721 safe transfer checks but produces a different onERC721Received return value.
Replace the returned bytes4 selector with keccak256 of a different method signature to change the return value.
Delete the assignment 'baseToken = _baseToken;' so baseToken remains its default zero-address.
Replace 'baseToken = _baseToken;' with 'baseToken = address(0);' so baseToken is always set to zero.
Replace 'baseToken = _baseToken;' with 'baseToken = _nft;' so baseToken is set to the NFT address.
Replace 'baseToken = _baseToken;' with 'baseToken = factory;' so baseToken is the factory address.
Delete the assignment `nft = _nft;` so the `nft` state variable is never set.
Replace `nft = _nft;` with `nft = address(0);` so the state variable is always set to the zero address instead of the provided argument.
Remove the assignment to changeFee so it retains its default (0) rather than the passed _changeFee.
Replace the feeRate assignment with a constant value of 0, so feeRate always initializes to 0 instead of the provided parameter.
Replace the feeRate assignment with a constant value of 5000, the maximum allowed fee rate.
Delete the feeRate assignment statement, leaving feeRate at its default value of 0.
Delete the assignment that sets `initialized = true`, so the contract remains uninitialized after the call.
Replace `initialized = true` with `initialized = false`, so the contract remains uninitialized after the call.
Delete the `if (initialized) revert AlreadyInitialized();` guard, allowing reinitialization that overwrites `initialized` to true again.
Change the assignment so payRoyalties is set to the negation of the provided _payRoyalties parameter
Assign payRoyalties to the constant true regardless of input parameter
Assign payRoyalties to the constant false regardless of input parameter
Remove the assignment to payRoyalties, leaving it at its default zero-value (false)
